name: Makaya McCraven
label: International Anthem
lede: McCraven records his band live, then takes the tapes home and cuts them up the way a hip-hop producer cuts samples. In These Times took seven years of that.

eras.title: A free-jazz drummer's kid in western Massachusetts
eras.text: Born in Paris, raised in western Massachusetts, where his father played free jazz and his mother sang Hungarian folk songs. By high school he was already mixing jazz with hip-hop.

years.h: A free-jazz drummer's son is born in Paris
years.p: His father is the drummer [[Stephen McCraven|c8dc6160-cdd0-479a-ade1-365a1732f693]]. His mother, Ágnes Zsigmondi, sang with the Hungarian band Kolinda, and the family settled around Amherst and Northampton, Massachusetts.
years.xp:
Stephen McCraven was mentored by the avant-garde figures [[Marion Brown|a16849a0-9329-4115-ba87-32ae7dcefca9]] and [[Archie Shepp|5ceff60b-8183-49bf-a855-328d3c172106]], according to Rolling Stone. Shepp taught near Amherst and [[Yusef Lateef|2968722f-03d8-4e2f-88bc-f9975f147503]] lived in the area, so the kid grew up around working jazz musicians, not the idea of them.

According to Wikipedia, at age 5 he played in his father's drum ensemble, the CMSS Bashers, next to his father's students.

years.h: At high school, Cold Duck Complex mixes jazz and hip-hop
years.p: In middle school he played in a band behind his mother's folk singing. Cold Duck Complex came next.
years.xp: Rolling Stone says a football-related hand injury in high school helped settle the question of whether he was an athlete or a musician.

years.h: UMass hands him DownBeat awards, not a diploma
years.p: He enrolled at UMass Amherst and won multiple DownBeat student awards, but never finished the degree. Steady local gigs won out.

eras.title: Chicago, a saxophonist's jam session, years as a sideman
eras.text: He follows his wife to Chicago and finds his people at a jam session run by a veteran saxophonist. Then comes a stretch as a sideman before anyone hears him as a leader.

years.cap: McCraven drumming at the Mo Jazz Cafe, Wilmington, Vermont
years.src: Rolling Stone · Wikipedia: Makaya McCraven · Passion of the Weiss
years.h: His wife's Northwestern job lands him at Fred Anderson's jam session
years.p: The professor Nitasha Tamar Sharma took the job. Anderson's Velvet Lounge session put McCraven in a room with players who knew both free jazz and hip-hop.
years.xp:
Rolling Stone dates the move to the mid-aughts and Wikipedia to 2007; Passion of the Weiss says 2006. McCraven told Rolling Stone the Velvet Lounge crowd was full of "young black musicians that had a reference for the avant-garde but also knew hip-hop."

In those early years Wikipedia lists him working with [[Bobby Broom|a5393110-610b-440c-8b90-6bca66be4739]], [[Corey Wilkes|71b849f0-f354-4006-96b1-c378633b178b]], [[Willie Pickens|535f3810-cf4b-4299-9c69-5dd1141df8b8]], [[Marquis Hill|8849eb24-3cff-4fa2-b750-acefc3dddf9d]] and [[Jeff Parker|4894f8eb-be75-4bd5-a3a3-7c20894439f9]], among others.

years.cap: McCraven on drums with the GMG Trio at an outdoor show, Frederick, Maryland, July 20, 2008
years.h: Before leading anything, he makes an album as GMG
years.p: Pianist Greg Spero and Graham Czach are the other two in the trio, and the trio travels: Frederick, Maryland, in July.

years.cap: McCraven on drums with the Bobby Broom Trio, INNtöne Jazzfestival, Austria
years.src: Wikipedia: Makaya McCraven · All About Jazz
years.h: Split Decision is the first record with his name on top
years.p: A trio album on the Chicago Sessions label, reviewed by All About Jazz in October 2012.

eras.title: Two guys start a label, and he starts tape
eras.text: Two guys launch International Anthem in Chicago and record a weekly jazz night. McCraven's method takes shape: record the band live, then cut it up in the studio.

years.h: A River North jazz night grows into International Anthem
years.p: Drummer Scottie McNiece started the night and brought in engineer David Allen to record it. The label's first release was [[Rob Mazurek|73c34525-f9c6-4c33-9abe-007748aaebe5]]'s Alternative Moon Cycles in December 2014.
years.xp: Per Wikipedia, McNiece and Allen set up the label in 2012 and launched it officially in 2014. It went on to release [[Jaimie Branch|8ff2bf9c-d1b6-4134-ae14-b837913c3dfd]], [[Irreversible Entanglements|ee3077be-0854-4603-876a-3e7e884bb462]], [[Ben LaMar Gay|2e0d2607-8a79-4123-93ff-0d12c1cef04e]], [[Angel Bat Dawid|b48d7422-680f-495e-9c98-fdbdfe76807a]] and [[Brandee Younger|61d68647-258e-43e2-942f-11321df5a96a]], and to share releases with Nonesuch, XL Recordings and Don Giovanni.

years.h: In the Moment starts as a weekly night and ends as an album
years.p: McCraven recorded the band live at International Anthem's weekly sessions, then edited the takes afterwards.
years.xp:
Rolling Stone describes the method as recording live sessions, then editing and overdubbing the material. McCraven calls it "a recontextualization of avant-garde concepts in jazz music," aimed at making it more approachable for a wider audience.

A remix companion, In the Moment Remix Tape, followed.

years.cap: McCraven on drums with the Marquis Hill Blacktet, BIM huis, Amsterdam
years.h: Most of 2016 goes to touring Europe
years.p: Wikipedia says he toured predominantly in Europe that year. In October 2017 he was in Amsterdam, drumming with trumpeter [[Marquis Hill|8849eb24-3cff-4fa2-b750-acefc3dddf9d]]'s Blacktet.

years.h: A single dive-bar night turns into Highly Rare
years.p: The record came from a single live performance. McCraven treated the tape as raw material, not a document.

eras.title: The method goes on the road
eras.text: He records bands in four cities and stitches them into one double album. The jazz press and the Gil Scott-Heron estate's label both notice.

years.src: Passion of the Weiss · Wikipedia: Makaya McCraven
years.h: Where We Come From puts Chicago and London on one mixtape
years.p: The London session included keyboardist [[Joe Armon-Jones|7f28f2b1-738b-41da-b168-9704dba00605]] and [[Kamaal Williams|fe5e321e-cbea-4b2d-8bfa-9c9074bed66d]].

years.h: Universal Beings gives each of four cities its own band
years.p: A 22-track double album recorded between August 2017 and January 2018 in New York, Chicago, London and Los Angeles.
years.xp:
According to Wikipedia, the New York sessions featured [[Brandee Younger|61d68647-258e-43e2-942f-11321df5a96a]] on harp, [[Joel Ross|6d09039b-3e1f-49ef-b8e3-b8b7267a8578]] on vibraphone and Dezron Douglas on bass; the Los Angeles sessions included [[Jeff Parker|4894f8eb-be75-4bd5-a3a3-7c20894439f9]], Josh Johnson and [[Carlos Niño|f6e8d274-e3f5-4491-bbea-bbf9a2119d95]]; London brought in [[Nubya Garcia|42dd1862-7255-47ed-8584-651abce3bf53]] and Ashley Henry. The album charted at No. 3 on Billboard's Jazz Albums chart and made NPR's top 50 of 2018.

McCraven told Rolling Stone he deliberately included women musicians throughout, and arranged the album as suites by city, presenting it as a snapshot of jazz now, not a revival.

years.h: Moving Cities pairs him with trumpeter Antoine Berjeaut
years.p: The collaboration came out on I See Colors.

years.big: "I didn't choose the record. The record chose me."
q: I didn't choose the record. The record chose me.
years.src: DownBeat · The Vinyl Factory · Wikipedia: International Anthem Recording Company
yt: Gil Scott-Heron, Makaya McCraven: I'm New Here
years.h: Richard Russell hands him Gil Scott-Heron's last album
years.p: Russell produced Scott-Heron's I'm New Here and asked McCraven for a remix project. McCraven layered live playing and samples from free-jazz records his parents appeared on underneath the vocals.
years.xp:
In DownBeat, McCraven said Russell approached him, and that he was "surprised and honored to be considered." He was drawn to the age in Scott-Heron's voice and the record's themes of going back home and coming full circle. The Vinyl Factory reports the samples came from free-jazz records his parents appeared on.

DownBeat calls it the first time McCraven reimagined another artist's whole album instead of remixing his own live tapes. It won a Libera Award for best jazz record, per Wikipedia's International Anthem page.

years.h: DownBeat's critics name him Rising Star drummer and producer
years.p: He took both categories in the 2020 poll, the same year he released Universal Beings E&F Sides.

eras.title: Blue Note, then seven years come due
eras.text: A detour into the Blue Note archive comes first, then the album he'd been carrying for years, with a string quartet, a harp and a newspaper office.

years.cap: Bassist Junius Paul, who plays on the record, at the Museum of Contemporary Art Chicago
years.h: Blue Note's catalog gets the McCraven treatment
years.p: Deciphering the Message runs thirteen tracks, with [[Joel Ross|6d09039b-3e1f-49ef-b8e3-b8b7267a8578]], [[Jeff Parker|4894f8eb-be75-4bd5-a3a3-7c20894439f9]], [[Junius Paul|e06be842-299d-4844-a019-fc377748cfdb]], [[Marquis Hill|8849eb24-3cff-4fa2-b750-acefc3dddf9d]] and Greg Ward.
years.xp: AllMusic's Thom Jurek wrote that McCraven's aim was "to point new listeners toward the originals," but the record stands on its own as a listen. Metacritic averaged seven critic scores to 78.

years.h: "Seventh String" goes out three months ahead of the album
years.p: It is the first song out from In These Times. The video went up June 21; Wikipedia gives June 23 as the announcement date.

years.cap: McCraven and his band on the outdoor stage at the Salt Shed, Chicago, August 2, 2022
years.src: Wikipedia: In These Times · Album of the Year · Spitfire Audio
years.h: After seven years, In These Times is done
years.p: Pitchfork gave it 8.0 and ranked it No. 18 of 2022. The title comes from a newspaper office where part of it was recorded.
years.xp:
Wikipedia counts five studios and four live spaces. McCraven told the Spitfire Audio blog the pieces came from live shows at Chicago's Symphony Center, the Co-Prosperity Sphere and the Walker Art Center in Minneapolis, plus a session at the offices of the In These Times newspaper, which gave the album its title. Post-production happened in hotel rooms, at home in Chicago, and at his mother-in-law's house in Hawaii once the pandemic began.

Guests include [[Jeff Parker|4894f8eb-be75-4bd5-a3a3-7c20894439f9]], [[Brandee Younger|61d68647-258e-43e2-942f-11321df5a96a]], Macie Stewart, Junius Paul, Marta Sofia Honer and Lia Kohl. Andy Cush's Pitchfork review gave it 8.0 and called the production more "deftly orchestrated and rhythmically complex" than McCraven's earlier work, per Album of the Year's summary. Metacritic averaged 11 reviews to 87; NPR Music placed it No. 7 on its 2022 list, Passion of the Weiss No. 3, and Stereogum named it the year's No. 1 jazz album.

years.cap: McCraven's drum kit on stage at North Sea Jazz Festival, Rotterdam, July 8, 2022
years.h: "Dream Another" comes with a zoopraxiscope-style animated video
years.p: The second single from In These Times, followed by "The Fours" on September 13.

eras.title: EPs folded into one record
eras.text: He tells NPR what he thinks of the word jazz, then gathers a run of EPs into a single release.

years.cap: McCraven at the kit, Strathmore Music Center, North Bethesda, Maryland
years.h: NPR asks what "jazz" means, and he answers
years.p: Asked about the word jazz, McCraven told NPR it means "a lot of different meanings to different people." He named [[Miles Davis|561d854a-6a28-4aa7-8c99-323e6ce46c2a]], [[Thelonious Monk|8e8c7417-c905-46b1-b42a-5260b4274ed4]] and [[Charles Mingus|f3b8e107-abe8-4743-b6a3-4a4ee995e71f]] as musicians who also pushed against the label.

years.cap: McCraven live at Club Soda, Montreal International Jazz Festival, June 2025
years.h: Off the Record folds four EPs into one album
years.p: It gathers PopUp Shop, Hidden Out!, Techno Logic and The People's Mixtape, and is his first major release since In These Times, per Wikipedia.
years.xp: The album features Jeff Parker, Benjamin J. Shepherd, Justefan, Junius Paul, Marquis Hill, Josh Johnson, Theon Cross, Ben LaMar Gay, Joel Ross and Jeremiah Chiu. Metacritic averaged seven critic scores to 83. The EPs were released separately on October 31, 2025.
